title: Top-K backpressure and continuation semantics for incremental rerank
creator: Rhea Kumar
description: Current rerank endpoint semantics around top_k, continuation tokens, and streaming incremental responses are inconsistent between SDKs and cause surprising client behavior under load. Clients either request a large candidate set upfront (high latency/cost) or try to stream incremental top results but encounter unstable ordering and duplicated items when continuation tokens are used. This ticket defines a concrete contract: how top_k interacts with candidate limits, how continuation tokens represent deterministic state, and how servers should apply backpressure and max-latency hints to trade quality vs. responsiveness.
problem_statement: Customers want a stable, low-latency rerank API that supports both one-shot ranking (give me top K) and incremental streaming (send best results as they become available). Current gaps: 1) 'top_k' is overloaded (some SDKs expect 'return_k' vs 'candidate_k'), 2) continuation tokens lack a canonical distinction between 'resume scanning' and 'resume returning results', and 3) the server performs unbounded candidate expansion causing latency spikes under burst traffic.
proposal_summary: Introduce explicit parameters: 'candidate_limit' (how many items to score internally), 'return_k' (how many final items to return), and optional 'max_latency_ms' as a backpressure hint. Replace opaque continuation tokens with a structured, opaque cursor that internally encodes 'last_scored_index' and 'seen_hashes' (server-side only); for clients this remains an opaque string but semantics are documented: resuming continues scanning the candidate set deterministically and avoids reordering of previously returned items. Streaming responses will include per-item stable_rank and provenance metadata. Default behavior: candidate_limit defaults to min(10*return_k, 1024) unless client overrides. Servers may early-stop scoring if max_latency_ms is reached, returning a partial but ordered top-N and a non-null continuation token.
acceptance_criteria: API surface adds 'candidate_limit', 'return_k', and optional 'max_latency_ms' fields to rerank request schema (backwards compatible defaults)
Continuation token is opaque to clients; documented server semantics guarantee no reordering of items already returned when a client resumes with the token
Streaming responses include stable_rank and source_provenance fields in structured output schema
Server honors 'max_latency_ms' as a best-effort backpressure signal and produces partial results + continuation token when time budget is exceeded
End-to-end tests for deterministic resumption under heavy load (integration fixture with 2k candidates) pass
Perf dashboard shows at least 20% reduction in P95 latency under burst traffic compared to current baseline when clients use candidate_limit or max_latency_ms
decisions: Rename external 'top_k' to 'return_k' in new API version to avoid ambiguity; keep legacy 'top_k' as alias for backward compatibility
Introduce 'candidate_limit' rather than exposing raw 'max_candidates' to control internal scoring explosion
Continuation token remains opaque; do not surface internal indexes or hashes in the token value, but document guarantee semantics clearly
Streaming items will carry 'stable_rank' (1..N) and 'provenance' (model_variant + candidate_source) for debugging and client-side deduplication
Make 'max_latency_ms' advisory only (best-effort) to avoid breaking SLOs; servers must still respect global SLO and can ignore advisory in overload situations
